Multiple times, I've been getting a NPE with empty stack trace, that I've been finally able to track down to the same `allocator.directBuffer()` call.

From comments above, I cannot understand how an error in handling these buffer could result in this NPE. 

I know that if I have some thread holding on a buffer, and then this buffer goes back to pool it may be possible that these buffer and the ByteBuf instance to be reused. In this case the first thread can get either 2 conditions: 
1. Touch/Read an invalid buffer (refCnt==0) and that should throw exception
2. Use the ByteBuf after it has been recycled. Probably lead to seeing corrupted data but ByteBuf should not throw exception

So far I haven't seen any refCnt exception or any data corruption. Still, I don't understand how either case should cause NPE.

Any clues / suggestions?
@merlimat do you run with assert's enabled ?
